editorial:
Ever felt like the invisible kid in class? You will totally relate to the main character here, a guy who is pretty much at the bottom of the social ladder. He is tired of being uncool and decides to do something wild to get the attention of the hottest girl in college. Since his parents are loaded, he decides to throw a massive, over-the-top birthday party at their fancy house while they are away. It is a classic setup that feels like a chaotic house party movie, filled with awkward moments, loud music, and plenty of social disasters that will make you laugh and cringe at the same time.

The acting is light and fun, and the pacing keeps things moving quickly so you never get bored. While some of the jokes are a bit predictable, the energy is high enough to make it work. If you love stories about underdogs trying to fit in, you should definitely give this one a shot. You can grab it by renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to really see the fancy house in all its glory.
endingExplained: After the party turns into absolute chaos, the main character realizes that trying to buy popularity with a big event was a mistake. Instead of the girl liking him for the party, he finds a real connection with her when he shows his true, awkward self. He learns that being honest is better than pretending to be cool. The movie wraps up with him feeling more confident and finally being accepted by his peers.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen comedies and underdog stories.
